A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniLIP research work. Their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. The complete documents were inspected, including v2's Appendices A–F; v1 ends with references and contains no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction, multimodal understanding, generation and editing results, together with reconstruction-training and dual-condition ablations in Tables 1–8.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for two model variants, expanded ablations, reconstruction-training curves, latency measurements and qualitative comparisons in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The two-stage self-distillation scheme and dual-condition architecture remain. v2 adds adversarial reconstruction training: a discriminator and BCE-based GAN loss weighted by 0.1, activated after 200k second-stage steps (Section 4.1, Appendix A.4). This refines the reconstruction objective without replacing the central method.

E1.justification: Editing pretraining replaces the UniWorld-V1 mixture sourced mainly from ImgEdit and SEED-X with the GPT-generated GPT-Image-Edit-1.5M corpus. v2 also adds TextVQA evaluation in Tables 1, 6 and 11. The main ImageNet, understanding, GenEval, WISE and ImgEdit benchmark coverage is retained; JourneyDB was already present in v1.

E2.justification: Generation comparisons add OpenUni-B/L, BLIP3-o-8B, SANA, ILLUME+, Tar and Show-o2, while removing quantitative Janus-1.3B and Janus-Pro-1B rows. Understanding comparisons also change, adding Tar and Janus-Pro-7B while removing InternVL2 and Qwen2-VL rows. The ImgEdit comparator set remains unchanged. These are changes in reported comparison membership, including appendix tables.

E3.justification: The reported second-stage reconstruction budget changes from 300k steps at 224 pixels plus 100k at 448 to 400k plus 100k; final generation/editing instruction tuning increases from 20k to 30k steps. v2 evaluates a larger InternVL3-2B/SANA-1.6B configuration, changes the reconstruction-ablation metrics, and introduces a single-A100, common-prompt latency comparison.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained reconstruction-strategy and dual-condition ablations, v2 tests reference/target encoder combinations (Table 8), removal of generation/editing training stages (Table 10), and distillation loss types and weights (Table 11). Training curves and comparative reconstruction, generation and editing cases in Figures 6–10 substantially expand diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. v2's new training curves show optimization trajectories, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: UniLIP-1B's main GenEval/WISE/ImgEdit results change from 0.87/0.53/3.62 to 0.88/0.56/3.81; v2 adds 3B results of 0.90/0.63/3.94. At 448 pixels, reconstruction rFID/PSNR/SSIM changes from 0.32/24.84/0.792 to 0.31/24.62/0.788. New ablation and latency results also appear. Training changes prevent treating these as controlled performance gains. v1 Table 8 additionally contains generation summary values, 0.86/0.44, inconsistent with its main benchmark tables.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the projected-feature tensor shape from H × W × d-hat to (H/p) × (W/p) × d-hat. This is a limited mathematical-definition correction. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract broadens the generation-performance framing from similarly sized unified models to explicit comparisons with larger models and introduces the 3B variant. The central contributions—unified CLIP representations, two-stage reconstruction training and dual conditioning—remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of how small feature changes accommodate pixel details, why training stages matter, and how distillation choices affect reconstruction and understanding (Appendix C). Encoder ablations support additional interpretations in Section 4.3. Appendix E newly identifies the 448-pixel resolution and model-scale limits and associated weaknesses in text rendering and editing.

D1.justification: Appendix A newly specifies projection layers and dimensions, 28-fold encoder downsampling with a 32-fold decoder and output interpolation, task-sampling ratios, classifier-free guidance dropout and scale, and adversarial-loss details. Appendix B documents variant-specific components. v2 also adds a reproducibility statement and a code/model access link. These substantially expand documentation without establishing that every newly disclosed setting changed.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds an instruction-guided editing discussion positioning UniLIP against approaches that still require VAE features. References add works including MoGAO, Show-o2, GPT-Image-Edit-1.5M, StyleGAN and LPIPS, while removing some background citations. The central positioning against quantized CLIP and diffusion-based reconstruction remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial portions of the introduction and related work are rewritten and condensed, with terminology standardized around multimodal hidden states. The exposition foregrounds the baseline comparison near the introduction and moves reconstruction to the beginning of the results discussion. Dedicated reproducibility and appendix sections further restructure the presentation.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 3 and 4 are restyled, and the separate generation/editing galleries are merged and partly replaced in Figure 5. v2 adds training plots and extensive comparison grids. Benchmark tables gain parameter columns and highlighted rows; GenEval/WISE are summarized jointly in the main text, with full category tables retained in the appendix. The baseline and ablation table structures are also revised.

improvement.justification: The encoder swaps and expanded training-stage and distillation ablations directly test central representation and training explanations that v1 left insufficiently examined. Appendix A fills substantial implementation gaps, and Appendix E states concrete applicability limits. These additions substantially strengthen validation and reproducibility. Changed training limits interpretation of score increases, and reporting flaws remain, including conflicting BLIP3-o labels in Tables 4 and 13, but these do not outweigh the stronger support for the core method.
